concepts.title: Ayurveda: The Science of Life
concepts.definition: Ayurveda, literally the science of life, is a holistic health system covering physical, physiological, psychological, environmental and ecological well-being. It aims not merely at curing disease but at preserving the health of the healthy and restoring balance in the ill.
concepts.key_idea: Science of life, not just medicine -- Ayurveda treats the whole person in a whole environment.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks107.txt opening (science of life, holistic health system, physical physiological psychological environmental ecological well being)
question_patterns: what does the word ayurveda literally mean

solution_steps.explain: Ayus means life, veda means knowledge -- ayurveda is the knowledge of life.
Its concerns run from body and mind to environment and ecology -- health as a whole system.
To protect the health of the healthy and to cure the diseases of the diseased -- prevention first.

concepts.title: Doshas, Balance and Diagnosis
concepts.definition: Ayurveda reads the body through the three doshas -- moving principles whose balance defines health and whose derangement defines disease. Diagnosis examines pulse, appearance, habits and history to find which dosha is disturbed; treatment then restores balance through diet, herbs, routine and therapies.
concepts.key_idea: Health is balance and disease is imbalance -- treatment means restoring the doshas, not just silencing symptoms.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks107.txt dosha sections (three doshas, balance and imbalance, diagnosis, treatment diet herbs routine)

solution_steps.explain: Three governing principles -- vata, pitta, kapha -- combine in each person in a characteristic pattern.
Through pulse and observation of body, appetite and habits, the physician locates the disturbed dosha.
Correct diet, herbs, regulated routine and therapies bring the doshas back to their healthy accord.

concepts.title: Ayurveda as a Contemporary Treasure House
concepts.definition: The chapter presents Ayurveda as a vast treasure house of ideas interesting and contemporary: emphasis on diet and lifestyle, prevention, plant-based remedies and ecological balance anticipates today's wellness concerns, and its classical texts remain subjects of active study and research.
concepts.key_idea: An ancient system speaking to modern worries -- lifestyle, prevention and ecology were Ayurveda's themes all along.
concepts.textbook_ref: keks107.txt contemporary sections (classical texts, plant remedies, prevention and lifestyle, research on ayurveda, relevance today)
question_patterns: why is ayurveda called relevant to modern times
in class 11 ayurveda chapter: what lifestyle advice of ayurveda is valued today
what role do plant based remedies play in ayurveda

solution_steps.explain: Classical compendia codified diagnosis, treatment and regimens that practitioners still consult.
Diet discipline, lifestyle balance and prevention match contemporary public-health advice.
Research on plant remedies and regimens continues testing and extending the treasure house.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A patient complains of poor digestion and disturbed sleep. Describe how an Ayurvedic physician would approach the case.

solution_template.explain: Pulse, tongue and history point to which dosha is deranged and by what habits.
Irregular meals and late nights are identified as the aggravating routine.
Corrected meal times, calming herbs and a regular sleep regimen aim at the imbalance itself.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why is a chapter written on an ancient system placed in a modern textbook? Argue using Ayurveda's contemporary relevance.

solution_template.explain: Diet, lifestyle, prevention and ecology are today's health headlines and Ayurveda's old themes.
Classical texts and plant remedies remain in use and under research.
The system's continuity and relevance justify its place in modern education.
